references.text: Leviticus describes the execution of the consecration of Aaron and his sons over seven days, as commanded in Exodus 29:35.
The introduction to the ordination ceremony for priests to be performed for Aaron and his sons.
Describes the filling-of-the-hand ritual (מִלֵּא יָד) which is central to the consecration of the priests.
The ram of consecration (אֵיל הַמִּלֻּאִים) is mentioned as part of the ceremony for filling the priests' hands.
Moses does what the Lord has commanded, parallel to the command to do everything according to God's instruction.
Ezekiel describes a seven-day purification period for the altar, similar to the consecration period for the priests.
The Epistle to the Hebrews mentions that there were many Levitical priests because death prevented them from continuing, in contrast to Christ's eternal priesthood.
28:41 explains the purpose of the seven days mentioned in 29:35.
30:30 confirms and summarizes the purpose of the ordination ritual (anointing and consecration) described in 29:35.
3:10 confirms the unique status and warning that follows from the ordination in 29:35.
29:24 is a specific part of the seven-day ceremony summarized in 29:35.
29:15 is a specific part of the ordination ritual summarized in 29:35.
29:4 is the first step in the seven-day ceremony summarized in 29:35.
